arguments.issue: Was the RPD’s application of paragraph 108(1)(a) of IRPA reasonable?
arguments.claim: The RPD’s decision that the Applicant ceased to be a Convention refugee by voluntarily re-availing himself of protection was reasonable and justified by evidence.
arguments.quote: The RPD’s decision is reasonable. It is justified by the evidence of the Applicant’s three trips to his country of nationality on a national passport between 2021 and 2023, and its reasoning follows the elements of the test for re-availment.

support.ref: Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, SC 2001, c 27, s 108(1)(a)
Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) v Nilam, 2017 FC 153

arguments.weak_spot: The Applicant may argue his humanitarian motive negates intention to re-avail protection.

arguments.issue: What is the standard of review for the RPD’s decision?
arguments.claim: The RPD’s decision is reviewed for reasonableness with deference to the specialized decision-maker.
arguments.quote: The RPD’s decision is reviewed for reasonableness. Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) v Vavilov, 2019 SCC 65 [Vavilov] at paras 10, 16 and 23–25.

support.ref: Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) v Vavilov, 2019 SCC 65
Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) v Khosa, 2009 SCC 12

arguments.weak_spot: Applicant may argue the decision was unreasonable or that evidence was misweighed.

arguments.issue: Did the RPD correctly apply the test for re-availment under paragraph 108(1)(a)?
arguments.claim: The RPD correctly applied the three-element test: voluntariness, intention, and actual obtaining of protection.
arguments.quote: Paragraph 108(1)(a) of IRPA provides that a claim for refugee protection shall be rejected... The test has three elements: voluntariness, intention and actual obtaining of protection.

support.ref: Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) v Nilam, 2017 FC 153

arguments.weak_spot: Applicant may argue presumption of intention was rebutted by his lack of knowledge.

arguments.issue: Is the Applicant’s humanitarian motive relevant to the intention element of re-availment?
arguments.claim: The RPD properly found the humanitarian motive irrelevant to intention; intention is presumed from voluntary acts and not displaced by lack of knowledge.
arguments.quote: The RPD considered the evidence and explained why the humanitarian motive was not relevant to the question of intention: see the RPD’s reasons at paragraphs 22–25.
arguments.weak_spot: Applicant may argue humanitarian reasons should negate intention to re-avail protection.

arguments.issue: Should the Court consider the Applicant’s new argument about subsection 108(2) of IRPA?
arguments.claim: The new argument about subsection 108(2) was not raised before the RPD and should not be heard on judicial review.
arguments.quote: To the extent the Applicant raises a new argument that the RPD should have applied subsection 108(2) of IRPA... that argument was not raised before the RPD and should not be heard on judicial review.

support.ref: Alberta (Information and Privacy Commissioner) v Alberta Teachers’ Association, 2011 SCC 61

arguments.weak_spot: Applicant may argue the new issue is central and should be considered despite not being raised earlier.
